prRef: https://github.com/TryGhost/Ghost/pull/15783 ("Added ability to send test email with chosen newsletter", merged 2023-01-09)
prTitle: Added ability to send test email with chosen newsletter
stackAndServices: JS/Node monorepo: Ember.js admin SPA (ghost/admin) -> Ghost core REST API (ghost/core, Express + Bookshelf/Knex over MySQL/SQLite) -> internal email-service package (ghost/email-service, EmailController) -> mega.js send pipeline -> Nodemailer/Mailgun transport (outbound egress to a configurable SMTP/Mailgun destination).
verdictBasis: The diff threads a new `newsletter` slug end-to-end and consistently: admin editor/modals/preview/email.js now loads the active-newsletters list (loadNewslettersTask), lets the user pick one (setNewsletter), and sends `newsletter: this.newsletter.slug` in the test-email POST body -> ghost/core/.../email-previews.js passes it through as a 4th arg -> mega.js `sendTestEmail(postModel, toEmails, memberSegment, newsletterSlug)` -> `getEmailData` resolves `models.Newsletter.findOne({slug: options.newsletterSlug})` instead of the post's bound/default newsletter -> rendered subject/HTML reflects the SELECTED newsletter, not the post's own. Unit tests (email-controller.test.js) were updated to mock a Newsletter model, consistent with the new lookup path. This is a coherent, non-vacuous discriminating claim (selection overrides the post's default newsletter) with a correct-looking negative (omit selection -> falls back to post's own/default newsletter, same as pre-PR). CONFESSION: I could not fully re-trace which exact API action the live in-iframe preview render (renderEmailPreview/_fetchEmailData) hits versus the test-send action -- email-controller.js's previewEmail was also patched with an OR-fallback (frame.options.newsletter ?? frame.data.newsletter), suggesting the render path is covered too, but I did not exhaustively confirm the exact frame field the GET preview call populates. NOT COVERED: whether a mismatch between the live preview shown to the user and the eventually-sent test email content is possible (twin-implementation risk, see breaks).
holds: Front-door walk is fully realizable with pure click/type/navigate/read: open editor -> Preview -> Email tab -> pick newsletter from dropdown -> pick member segment -> type test-email address -> click Send. No forged requests needed.

This is a clean EGRESS-effect case per P'(b): the essence is an outbound test email to a user-typed address (their own inbox) via a configurable mail transport (SMTP/Mailgun) -- CONJURE-REAL is legitimate by pointing the sandbox's mail config at a local SMTP catcher (e.g. Maildev/MailHog) the harness controls, which is a genuine user-configurable destination, not a fixed-vendor stub -> avoids automatic CND.

The discriminating claim is genuinely non-trivial and avoids FW-3 (vacuous claims): 'test email works' was already true pre-PR; the actual claim (selected-newsletter content overrides the post's bound newsletter) only becomes true after this diff, so a pre/post-PR run would visibly diverge -- good compile target.

Async newsletter-list load (loadNewslettersTask) and the `if (this._previewIframe)` re-render guard create a real flakiness surface (select-before-load races) that P'(d)'s k/N-fresh-world reproduction requirement is specifically designed to catch -- the mechanism does its intended job here rather than being decorative.

No persisted-state mutation occurs on test-send (it's read + egress only), so mutation-attribution calibration (1.1/1.2) is correctly a no-op for this feature and the verdict correctly rests entirely on the egress ledger (1.5) rather than forcing a spurious write-set check.

breaks.detail: The feature is delivered by two independently-written newsletter-resolution snippets: email-controller.js's previewEmail (frame.options.newsletter ?? frame.data.newsletter, used by the live in-iframe render) and mega.js's sendTestEmail (options.newsletterSlug, threaded only from the POST body via email-previews.js, used by the actual test-send). A claim compiler asked for 'the ONE discriminating claim' from a PR titled 'send test email with chosen newsletter' will naturally pick the punchiest verb -- clicking Send and inspecting the delivered mail -- and never separately drives/inspects the live preview iframe's rendered HTML. Nothing in P' forces coverage of BOTH code paths behind one user-visible feature; they can silently diverge (e.g. preview shows newsletter A's design while the actually-sent test email uses newsletter B) and a WORKS verdict would still issue because only the send leg was in the compiled claim.
breaks.fix: For any feature where the diff touches >1 independently-coded resolution path for the same user-visible selection, require the pre-registered claim set to include at least one check per distinct backend code path reachable from the front-door action set, not just the path the loudest verb implies.

breaks.detail: P'(b)'s egress content-binding is written for a fresh, same-window-created entity. Here the 'entity' whose content must show up in the egress payload is a Newsletter -- a pre-existing CONFIG row, not something created inside the action window. If two newsletters at world-build time happen to share similar names/branding (or the harness reuses fixture newsletters across many test runs), a content-match could be a false positive (matching stale content from a prior run, or matching a substring shared with the site title). The theory doesn't spell out that pre-existing config entities used for content-binding must be seeded with a fresh per-run randomized marker (e.g. a UUID embedded in the newsletter name/header) immediately before the walk, the same way a freshly-created row would be.
breaks.fix: Extend 1.5 (EGRESS effect check): when content-binding targets a pre-existing config/reference row rather than a row created in-window, require the harness to inject a fresh randomized marker into that row via a front-door-adjacent action (e.g. admin settings edit) as part of world setup, and bind on the marker, not on the row's semantic name.

breaks.detail: FW-11's quantifier lint (>=2 distinct in-scope instantiations not the configuring actor, +1 out-of-scope negative) was designed around actor-shadow collapse (e.g. owner vs. other users). Here the 'any newsletter' quantifier ranges over a config entity, not an actor, so the 'not the configuring actor' clause is vacuously satisfied and doesn't actually rule out the realistic failure mode (e.g. an implementation that always renders the FIRST item in newslettersList regardless of user selection). The lint as worded gives a false sense of coverage for this PR unless the >=2-instantiation requirement is explicitly reinterpreted as 'not the default/first-returned item' rather than 'not the configuring actor'.
breaks.fix: State FW-11's non-actor clause more generally: the required 2nd instantiation must not equal whatever the naive/degenerate implementation would default to (first list item, default row, etc.), not only 'not the configuring actor'.

sonnetDifficulty: The hard part for me was NOT executing the mechanics of P' (front-door walk, egress carve-out, quantifier lint) -- those apply mechanically once you have the right claim. The hard part was diff-archaeology: finding the ONE non-vacuous discriminating claim required tracing four files (admin component -> REST endpoint -> mega.js -> email-service's email-controller.js) and specifically noticing that memberSegment already existed pre-PR (so a naive read of the diff could mistake 'segment' for the discriminating axis) while newsletter was the actually-new, actually-discriminating parameter. I nearly stopped after mega.js and almost missed that email-controller.js has an entirely separate (and differently-shaped) resolution snippet for the preview-render path, which is what surfaced the twin-implementation-drift vector. A shallower pass by me -- or a less careful agent -- would very plausibly have compiled the vacuous claim 'sending a test email works' (already true pre-PR) or stopped at one code path and missed the second entirely. This is exactly the genius-dependence risk the task warns about: nothing in the mechanical checklist (1.1-1.5) tells you to go hunt for a second, differently-coded fork of the same user-visible behavior -- that step is manual diff literacy, not process.
newVectors: Twin-implementation drift (named above): a single user-visible feature backed by >1 independently-coded resolution path in the diff, where the mandated 'ONE discriminating claim' can cover only one path, silently leaving the other(s) completely unverified -- distinct from FW-12/FW-14 because it's not about fixture-vs-prod divergence or config drift, it's about the compiled CLAIM SET's coverage of the DIFF's own internal forks.

Egress content-binding on pre-existing/config rows (rather than in-window-created rows) needs an explicit freshness-marker requirement that P'(b) as written doesn't state, or content-matches risk false positives across repeated runs or coincidental substring overlap.
openQuestions: Does the live in-iframe preview render (renderEmailPreview / _fetchEmailData in admin's email.js) actually hit email-controller.js's previewEmail with frame.data.newsletter set from the selected newsletter, or a different, untouched code path? I could not fully confirm this from the diff hunks alone.
Is there any audit/event log row written when a test email is sent (for mutation-attribution calibration), or is this genuinely a zero-DB-write, egress-only action as the diff suggests?

Does Ghost's test suite/CI for this PR exercise a real SMTP transport in an integration test, or only unit-level mocks of Newsletter.findOne -- relevant to how much CONJURE-REAL work would be needed to stand up the egress ledger.
conjureFeasibility: REAL is plausible and preferable here: Ghost is a single self-hostable Node/Ember app (yarn dev / docker) with a configurable mail transport, so the sandbox can point mail config at a local SMTP catcher (Maildev/MailHog) as the 'controlled receiver' required by the EGRESS carve-out -- this is a genuine user-configurable destination, not a fixed-vendor stub, so it need not force CND. Two newsletters and one post are cheap to seed via the real Admin UI/API (front-door-adjacent, not raw DB fixture injection) at world-build time, which also lets the freshness-marker fix above be applied. Nothing here needs to be DOUBLED or SEALED-OUT beyond the mail transport itself, and nothing structurally forces CND except the two open questions above (preview-path coverage, audit-log existence) which are answerable by reading a bit more code, not by a fundamental environment limitation.
compiledPromise: Discriminating claim: "When an author selects a non-default newsletter N (from the site's active newsletters) in the post editor's Email Preview modal and clicks Send test email, the delivered test email's subject/HTML content reflects newsletter N's design/branding -- NOT the post's own bound newsletter or the site default." Negative: "When no newsletter is explicitly selected (or the post's own bound newsletter is left as-is), the delivered test email is identical to pre-PR behavior (uses the post's bound newsletter, falling back to the site default) -- selection has no effect unless actively changed." Compiled matrix requires >=2 distinct newsletters instantiated (not merely the site's single default) plus 1 out-of-scope negative (archived/inactive newsletter must NOT appear as selectable, and must not be reachable as a selection at all).
